scope.summary: Create the non-product Phase 0D benchmark contract and executable admission gates that prove equivalent work before any Ferric-versus-reference timing sample can influence a performance claim.
in_scope: Define strict versioned benchmark-manifest, raw-sample, normalized-observation, environment-profile, equality-admission, rejection, and aggregate-report schemas.

Pin exact Ferric commit/build/profile/features/allocator, optional comparison artifact identity, FFmpeg/ffprobe identity, transport/archive/challenge identities, fixture/corpus hashes, and process topology.

Define equality predicates for source graph, request sequence, bytes/fragments, selected streams, output and ffprobe facts, metadata/sidecars, archive action, validation, failure class, cache/network state, and process topology before timing.

Define Windows and Unix host profiles covering machine, OS, filesystem, storage, antivirus/security state, power/governor, CPU affinity, memory pressure, and cold/warm cache policy without hardcoded machine-local paths.
Define randomized paired order, warmup, repetitions, raw-sample retention, outlier/noise policy, distributions, 95-percent confidence bounds, no-regression admission, and improvement thresholds.

Implement deterministic negative fixtures that reject cheaper work, mismatched provenance, asymmetric cache state, changed topology, missing raw samples, single-mean reports, and structurally self-validating claims.
Keep canonical proof Ferric-owned and executable with Python, yt-dlp, companion assets, cloud services, and optional comparison tools absent.
Expose the exact no-context command, inputs, outputs, limits, failure diagnostics, and recovery path through the non-shipped xtask help and machine-readable gate output.
non_goals: Claiming Ferric is faster, non-regressing, parity-complete, product-ready, or release-ready.
Executing or completing the Phase 1 or Phase 2 production runtime slices.
Selecting a new benchmark dependency, hosted service, Python tool, shell-composed runner, or native runtime without separate authority.
Using live internet measurements as canonical evidence.
Allowing an optional external comparison executable to become a build, test, verification, package, release, or runtime prerequisite.
Replacing raw samples and equality observations with one aggregate mean or a self-authored PASS field.

acceptance_matrix.requirement: Strict versioned schemas bind every run and sample to exact source, build, toolchain, features, optional comparison artifact, FFmpeg/ffprobe, dependency decisions, fixture/corpus, host, filesystem, cache, process-topology, and metric identities; unknown fields, missing identities, duplicate sample IDs, and mismatched manifests are rejected.

A public admission boundary compares concrete normalized observations and rejects deliberately cheaper or different work before statistics, including lower-quality selection, omitted metadata/sidecar/archive/validation work, changed cache state, different request sequence, shifted subprocess work, and changed process topology.

Windows and Unix profile manifests define replayable host and environment conditions, bounded preparation and cleanup, cold/warm policy, noise thresholds, measurement availability, and explicit unsupported metrics without hardcoded paths or silent substitution.

The statistical contract retains raw samples and enforces randomized paired order, declared warmup, minimum repetitions, outlier/noise policy, distributions, and 95-percent confidence bounds; a single mean, missing samples, unstable noise, and a confidence interval crossing its declared gate cannot PASS.

Machine-readable reports preserve the weakest executed proof class, separate total-system, Ferric, FFmpeg, and other authorized worker costs, disclose unavailable metrics and residual uncertainty, and cannot promote structural or declaration-only evidence to behavioral or performance PASS.

Canonical architecture, PR, and triggered benchmark/deep gates execute the equality and statistics validators plus isolated counterfactual fixtures; independent adversarial review finds no unresolved false-equivalence, provenance, topology, noise, or self-validation path.
